title.narrative: Meeting the hygienic needs of the affected population from the number of women, girls and adults with reduced mobility in the border communities of Chernihiv region

description.narrative: ltpgtAs part of the project, we aim to provide humanitarian aid to the affected population of 4 border communities in Chernihiv region, namely:ltbrgt- 5273 Menstrual Hygiene Management Kits for women and girls (two-month supply)ltbrgt- 600 People with Special Needs Hygiene Kit for the adult population with limited mobility and immobility (two-month supply).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe target communities include the following urban territorial communities:ltbrgt1. Koriukivka district: Snovsk, Koriukivka communities (bordering Russia).ltbrgt2. Novhorod-Siverskyi district: Semenivka community (bordering Russia).ltbrgt3. Chernihiv district: Horodnia community (the only one in Ukraine bordering Russia and Belarus).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe total population of the four communities is 74.3 thousand, including more than 4 thousand IDPs. Among them, 19,400 people live within the 20 km zone from the border, which is 26%. Almost 41% of settlements are located in the 20 km border zone, namely 95 out of 232 settlements in these communities. The total length of their border with Russia exceeds 260 km. In April 2022, all communities were de-occupied. After the retreat of Russian troops, this border has effectively become a demarcation line.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThree of the four communities (Snovsk, Horodnia, and Semenivka) are listed as territorial communities located in the area of military (combat) operations or under temporary occupation, encirclement (blockade).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe administrative centers of these communities are located at a distance of 12-32 km from the border with Russia, and all are within the range of artillery fire. Almost daily, Russians shell the border villages with mortars and cannon artillery. So far, 380 houses in these communities have been damaged, creating abnormal living conditions for the residents. People continuously relocate from areas under fire. The border villages are gradually disappearing. The majority of the population moves deeper into their own and neighboring communities. This constant security threat significantly affects the resource situation and the level of basic needs of residents of the Chernihiv border region, especially vulnerable categories such as women and girls, the elderly, IDPs, and people with disabilities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTherefore, the population of these communities requires ongoing assistance and support, particularly those residing in rural areas.ltspangt lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtIn addition, the situation with access to basic needs for the rural population of the target communities is further complicated by the lack of transportation links between community centers and rural areas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
